summary: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indology, archaeology, and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies and under George de Roerich. He held long-term posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences and Moscow State University.

Gritli von Mitterwallner was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. She completed her Dr. phil. and habilitation at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett. He became an assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong around 2003.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He worked as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from circa 1986 to 2000 and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2005.
Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and served as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies figure who earned a law degree at the University of Tokyo and studied under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. He lectured at the Tokyo University Buddhist Association and Toho Gakuin.

Gudrun Bühnemann is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner. After research fellowships in India and Japan, she was appointed Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate under Jens-Uwe Hartmann at the University of Munich. In 2026, her positions were attested at the University of Munich, Göttingen Academy, and IIBS.
Gunapala Dharmasiri was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Stig Wikander. She held a post at Uppsala University from circa 1970 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from 1926 to 1933 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney. His traditional teachers included Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin, and he was abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery in 2013.

Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyo Mitomo. He also studied under traditional teacher Sheng Yen and several other mentors, including Hoyo Watanabe and Zensho Kitagawa.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He taught religion at Columbia from 1988 to 1999 and held the Kundan Kaur Kapany Chair at UC Santa Barbara from 1999 to 2015.

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Leiden University. He served at Utrecht University from 1924 to 1957 and the University of Amsterdam from 1935 to 1944.
Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart. He was attested in 2014 as a Senior Teaching Fellow at SOAS.

Gustaf John Ramstedt was a scholar of linguistics and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki, where he later held a post from circa 1903 to 1941, alongside a post at the University of Tokyo from 1920 to 1929.

Gustav Haloun was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady at Leipzig University. He directed at the University of Göttingen from 1931 to 1938 and held the Chair of Chinese Language and History at the University of Cambridge from 1938 to 1951.

Gustav Mensching was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied under Rudolf Otto. He held posts at the University of Latvia from 1927 to 1936 and the University of Bonn starting in 1936.

Gustav Roth was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Munich. He held a post at the University of Göttingen from 1965 to 1981 and directed the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from 1982 to 1985.
